executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across Europe and the Americas. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas region represents the most critical select agent concern, with both November 2025 and March 2026 updates indicating sustained circulation in animal reservoirs with pandemic spillover potential. Additional elevated concerns include mpox transmission in the Americas, yellow fever activity, and a resurgent pertussis wave. Respiratory virus co-circulation including seasonal influenza and RSV adds further burden to health systems entering mid-2026.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues active circulation in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, concurrent with mpox, yellow fever, dengue, and pertussis surges demanding sustained multi-pathogen surveillance and response capacity.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
Ongoing animal reservoir activity with documented zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring heightened surveillance at human-animal interface
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface; enforce strict biosafety protocols at BSL-3 level; expedite antiviral stockpiling and pre-pandemic vaccine preparedness; alert veterinary and public health authorities across affected countries

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained community spread following global emergency designation
Risk of clade Ib introduction from African epicenters remains a concern
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs; enhance genomic sequencing to distinguish clades; reinforce cross-border surveillance and reporting mechanisms

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases in the Americas
Ongoing epizootics in non-human primates serving as amplifying hosts
Risk of urban transmission in unvaccinated populations in endemic areas
threats.action: Intensify vaccination coverage in at-risk and border populations; enhance non-human primate mortality surveillance as early warning signal; enforce vaccination requirements for travelers to endemic zones

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 documenting sustained high case burden
Record or near-record case counts continuing trend from 2024 hyperepidemic year
Expansion of Aedes aegypti vector range increasing geographic risk
threats.action: Maintain vector control operations and eliminate breeding sites; strengthen clinical management capacity for severe dengue; promote community-based surveillance and public awareness campaigns

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO reports issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating resurgent wave
Sustained inter-season circulation affecting all age groups
Potential waning vaccine immunity contributing to outbreaks in vaccinated populations
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates and implement catch-up immunization; prioritize Tdap boosters for pregnant women and healthcare workers; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity for clinical cases

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: Multiple PAHO and ECDC alerts across November 2025 through May 2026 covering both hemispheres
PAHO January 2026 alert flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing healthcare systems
Southern hemisphere 2026 season onset confirmed by April 2026 PAHO alert
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination ahead of seasonal peaks; ensure adequate antiviral treatment stockpiles; strengthen ICU surge capacity planning for co-epidemic respiratory burden

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Risk of importation into sub-optimally vaccinated communities
Potential for outbreak amplification in areas with COVID-19-era vaccination gaps
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments and targeted catch-up campaigns; strengthen case-based surveillance and rapid response to confirmed cases; enforce vaccination requirements at international borders

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 flagging active transmission
Expanding Aedes vector distribution increasing risk beyond historically endemic zones
Co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis and case management
threats.action: Enhance clinical differentiation from dengue through laboratory confirmation; strengthen vector surveillance and control; increase physician awareness of atypical presentations and chronic arthralgia sequelae

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is the primary BSL-3 select agent identified across these reports, flagged in two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) for the Americas region. H5N1 is classified as a Tier 1 select agent with significant pandemic potential due to its high case fatality rate in humans and ongoing evolution in diverse animal reservoirs including wild birds, poultry, and mammals. Sustained circulation in the Americas with documented zoonotic spillover risk warrants Critical threat classification. No BSL-4 agents were explicitly identified in the available report titles and descriptions.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis with potential reduced vaccine susceptibility suggested by resurgent waves in vaccinated populations warrants molecular epidemiological investigation
No explicit AMR-specific alerts identified in available report titles; ECDC weekly threat reports likely contain AMR signals requiring full text review
emergingPatterns: Dual-hemisphere simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation stressing health systems across both the Americas and Europe in overlapping seasons
Persistent H5N1 activity in Americas animal reservoirs over a multi-month period with zoonotic risk escalation
Post-pandemic resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including pertussis and measles reflecting immunization program disruptions
Arboviral disease expansion (dengue and chikungunya) into new geographic areas driven by climate-related vector range shifts
Continued mpox community transmission in the Americas despite global emergency response measures indicating endemic establishment risk
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse flagged as an emerging non-infectious public health alert in the Americas reflecting expanding pharmacovigilance mandate for health authorities
